title: HTTP Methods, Status Codes and Headers: Quick Revision
summary: Revision notes on what GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE mean, which methods are safe or idempotent, how status code classes work, and the headers worth knowing. It ends with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: The Request-Response Mental Model
points: HTTP is stateless request-response: the client sends method + URL + headers + optional body, and the server returns status line + headers + optional body
The method says what to do, the URL says to which resource, the status code says how it went
Resources are nouns in the URL (/users/42); methods are the verbs, so avoid /getUser or /deleteUser
Each request is self-contained: the server keeps no memory between requests, so auth and context travel in headers (Authorization, Cookie)
Method semantics are a contract that clients, caches and proxies rely on, such as retrying or caching, so breaking it causes real bugs

chapters.title: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE Semantics
points: GET reads a resource and has no body semantics: GET /users/42 returns it, and parameters go in the query string
POST creates or triggers an action on a collection: POST /users returns 201 Created with a Location header, and the server picks the new ID
PUT replaces the whole resource at a known URL: PUT /users/42 with the full body, omitted fields are reset or removed, and it creates the resource if missing
PATCH applies a partial update: PATCH /users/42 {"email":"a@b.com"} changes only the sent fields
DELETE removes the resource and returns 204 No Content (or 200 with a body); deleting an already-deleted resource gives the same end state

chapters.title: Safe and Idempotent Methods
points: Safe means the method does not change server state: GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are safe, so crawlers and prefetchers may call them freely
Idempotent means that repeating the same request N times leaves the same server state as sending it once
Idempotent methods are GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE; POST and PATCH are not guaranteed idempotent
Safe is a subset of idempotent: every safe method is idempotent, but PUT and DELETE are idempotent and not safe
Idempotency tells clients what is safe to auto-retry after a timeout, and retrying POST (payments) needs an Idempotency-Key header to avoid duplicates

chapters.title: Status Code Classes and the Common Codes
points: Classes: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error (fix the request), 5xx server error (server failed, a retry may work)
2xx to know: 200 OK, 201 Created (with Location), 204 No Content (success, empty body)
3xx to know: 301 permanent redirect, 302/307 temporary redirect (307 keeps the method), 304 Not Modified (use the cache copy)
4xx to know: 400 bad input, 401 not authenticated, 403 authenticated but forbidden, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 422 validation failed, 429 rate limited
5xx to know: 500 unhandled server error, 502 bad gateway (upstream sent a bad response), 503 unavailable or overloaded (can send Retry-After), 504 gateway timeout

chapters.title: Headers That Matter and Common Mistakes
points: Content-Type describes the body you send (application/json) and Accept says which format you want back; a mismatch gives 415 Unsupported Media Type or 406 Not Acceptable
Authorization: Bearer <token> carries credentials on every request, and a missing or invalid one should give 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header
Cache-Control (max-age, no-store) with ETag and If-None-Match lets the server answer 304 when nothing changed, and If-Match on PUT gives optimistic locking (412 on conflict)
Location points to the new or redirected resource, and Retry-After says how long to wait after 429 or 503
Common mistakes: returning 200 with an error body, using GET to change data, using POST for everything, returning 500 for bad client input, and mixing up 401 and 403

chapters.title: HTTP Methods and Status Codes Cheat Sheet
points: Method table: GET read (safe, idempotent), POST create/action (neither), PUT replace (idempotent), PATCH partial update (not guaranteed idempotent), DELETE remove (idempotent)
Success codes by method: GET 200, POST 201, PUT 200 or 204, PATCH 200, DELETE 204
Error codes in one line: 400 bad request, 401 who are you, 403 not allowed, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 422 invalid, 429 slow down, 500 server bug, 502/504 upstream, 503 overloaded
Headers in one line: Content-Type, Accept, Authorization, Cache-Control, ETag/If-None-Match, Location, Retry-After
curl: curl -i https://api.x.com/users/42 for GET, and curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"a"}' https://api.x.com/users for POST
